h: Torah Brings Salvation to Past and Future

p: "הִנֵּה אֵל יְשׁוּעָתִי וְגוֹמֵר" (יְשַׁעְיָה יב, ב) –
— Behold, God is my salvation, etc. (Isaiah 12:2)—
הוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (חֵלֶק א, קעד סוֹף עַמּוּד א):
— follows what is written in the holy Zohar on this portion (Part I, 174a end):
"לְמָעוֹז – דָּא הוּא תּוּקְפָּא דְּאִית בֵּיהּ יְשׁוּעוֹת, דִּכְתִיב: 'וּמָעוֹז יְשׁוּעוֹת מְשִׁיחוֹ הוּא' (תְּהִלִּים כח, ח)".
— "'A stronghold'—this is the divine power wherein salvations reside, as it is written: 'and He is a saving stronghold to His anointed'."
וְהַמְּכוּוָּן עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה כא, ד):
— And the intention is based on Vayikra Rabbah (21:4):
"יִשְׁעִי – בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים",
— “‘My salvation’—this refers to Yom Kippur,”
שֶׁעִיקַּר יְשׁוּעָה – תִּיקּוּן הֶעָבָר, מְחִילַת עֲווֹנוֹת.
— for the essence of salvation is the rectification of the past and the pardon of sins.

וְאָמַר (בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ שָׁם): "וְהֵיךְ יִתְקַף בַּר נָשׁ בֵּיהּ בְּקֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא? יִתְקַף בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא, דְּכָל מַאן דְּאִתְתַּקַּף בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא – אִתְתַּקַּף בְּאִילָנָא דְּחַיֵּי", עַיֵּין שָׁם.
— And the Zohar asks: "And how can a man grasp hold of the Holy One? Let him grasp hold of the Torah, for whoever grasps the Torah grasps the Tree of Life," see there.

paragraphs.text: Vayikra Rabbah 21:4: “The Rabbis interpreted the verse regarding the New Year and Yom Kippur; ‘my light,’ (Psalms 27:1) on the New Year, ‘and my salvation’ (Psalms 27:1) on Yom Kippur. Whom shall I fear? (The Lord is the stronghold (maoz) of my life)’ (Psalms 27:1) – ‘The Lord is my strength (ozi) and my song’ (Exodus 15:2). ‘When evildoers approach me’ (Psalms 27:2) – these are the guardian angels of the nations of the world. ‘To consume my flesh’ (Psalms 27:2) – because the guardian angels of the nations of the world come and denounce Israel before the Holy One blessed be He, and say before Him: ‘Master of the universe, these are idol worshippers and those are idol worshippers. These engage in forbidden sexual relations and those engage in forbidden sexual relations. These are shedders of blood and those are shedders of blood. Why are these descending to Gehenna and those are not descending to Gehenna?’ ‘My foes and my adversaries are mine’ (Psalms 27:2). There are three hundred and sixty-five days in the solar calendar. The numerical value of hasatan is three hundred and sixty-four. All the days of the year, the accuser (hasatan) denounces, but on Yom Kippur he does not denounce. Israel said before the Holy One blessed be He: ‘If a camp’ – of Samael – ‘besieges me, my heart will not fear…(in this (bezot) I will put my trust)’ (Psalms 27:2) – because you promised me: ‘With this (bezot) Aaron shall come into the Sanctuary’ (Leviticus 16:3).”

p: וּבְשַׁבָּת כָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל עוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה,
— And on Shabbat every Jew is engaged in Torah study,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (רֵישׁ סֵדֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה): "שַׁבָּת יֵעָשֶׂה כֻּלָּהּ תּוֹרָה",
— as written in Seder Eliyahu Rabbah (ch. 1): "Shabbat shall be made entirely Torah",
וְכָל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל אִתְתַּקַּף בַּתּוֹרָה וּבְקֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא.
— and every Jew grasps hold of the Torah and the Holy One, blessed be He.
וְאָמַר (שָׁם סֵדֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה): "'יָמִים יֻצָּרוּ וְלוֹ אֶחָד בָּהֶם' (תְּהִלִּים קלט, טז) – זֶה יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל";
— And Seder Eliyahu expounds: "'The days were fashioned, and one of them was His'—this is the Sabbath day unto Israel";
וְדִקְדֵּק "בָּהֶם" דַּיְיקָא – שֶׁקְּדוּשַׁת הַשַּׁבָּת מוֹפִיעַ בְּכָל שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה,
— and pinpointed "among them" (bahem)—teaching that the holiness of Shabbat radiates into all six weekdays;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָאֲרִ"י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה:
— as the holy Ari wrote:
שֶׁנִּשְׁאָר רְשִׁימוּ בִּתְלָתָא יוֹמָא דִּבְתַר שַׁבַּתָּא מִשַּׁבָּת הֶעָבָר,
— that an impression remains throughout the first three days following Shabbat from the past Sabbath,
וּבִתְלָתָא דִּקְמֵי שַׁבַּתָּא מוֹפִיעַ מִקְּדוּשַׁת שַׁבָּת הַבָּא.
— and during the three days preceding Shabbat illumination shines from the upcoming Sabbath.

Although you do work throughout the six days, Shabbat should be made entirely Torah. Therefore they said: A person should rise early and study on Shabbat, go to the synagogue and house of study, read Torah and study the Prophets, and afterwards go home to eat and drink.”

h: The Written Torah Rectifies the Past

p: וְעַל כֵּן אוֹמְרִים בְּמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת: "הִנֵּה אֵל יְשׁוּעָתִי" –
— Therefore we recite at the conclusion of Shabbat: "Behold, God is my salvation"—
יְשׁוּעָה עַל הֶעָבָר,
— salvation over the past,
שֶׁבְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת עַל יְדֵי שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת, אֲפִילּוּ עוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כֶּאֱנוֹשׁ מוֹחֲלִין לוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּגְּמָרָא (שַׁבָּת קיח עַמּוּד ב).
— since on Shabbat, through Sabbath observance, even an idolater like Enosh is forgiven (Shabbat 118b).
"אֶבְטַח וְלֹא אֶפְחָד" – אַף בְּשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה.
— "I will trust and not be afraid"—even throughout the six working days.
"כִּי עָזִּי וְזִמְרָת יָהּ ה' וַיְהִי לִי לִישׁוּעָה",
— "For the Lord God is my strength and song, and He is become my salvation",
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "טוֹב ה' לְמָעוֹז" (נַחוּם א, ז),
— and as written: "Hashem is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble",
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁדָּרַשׁ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ: שֶׁהוּא הַתְּקִיפוּת בַּתּוֹרָה וּבְקֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא,
— which the Zohar expounds: that this stronghold is the fierce cleaving unto Torah and the Holy One,
וְהוּא תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב, שֶׁהוּא מוֹעִיל לְתַקֵּן כָּל הֶעָבָר.
— namely the Written Torah, which possesses the power to rectify the entire past.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה לח, ד): "'קְחוּ עִמָּכֶם דְּבָרִים' (הוֹשֵׁעַ יד, ג) – וְאֵין דְּבָרִים אֶלָּא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי",
— As written in Shemot Rabbah (38:4): "'Take with you words'—and words are nothing other than words of Torah",
שֶׁזֶּה מוֹעִיל לְתַקֵּן הֶעָבָר, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם: "וַאֲנִי מוֹחֵל עַל כָּל עֲווֹנוֹתֵיכֶם".
— which avails to cleanse the past, Hashem declaring: "and I forgive all your iniquities".
וּכְתִיב: "וּלְכָל בְּשָׂרוֹ מַרְפֵּא" (מִשְׁלֵי ד, כב) –
— And it is written: "and health to all his flesh" (Proverbs 4:22)—
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה רְפוּאָה, וּמוֹעִיל לְתַקֵּן הַכֹּל;
— meaning that words of Torah are healing medicine, rectifying everything;
וְאַף לַפְּגָם שֶׁנִּמְנַע הַתְּשׁוּבָה בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א, ריט עַמּוּד ב),
— and even regarding the blemish of the Covenant where ordinary repentance is barred in the Zohar (I 219b),
אָמַרְנוּ שֶׁרַק תְּשׁוּבָה בִּלְבַד אֵינוֹ מוֹעִיל, אֲבָל עַל יְדֵי תּוֹרָה מוֹעִיל תְּשׁוּבָה;
— we explained that repentance alone is insufficient, but when accompanied by Torah, repentance avails;
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה יח עַמּוּד א): "בְּזֶבַח וּבְמִנְחָה אֵינוֹ מִתְכַּפֵּר, אֲבָל מִתְכַּפֵּר הוּא בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה".
— in the manner of Rosh Hashanah (18a): "Through animal sacrifice it is not atoned, but it is atoned through words of Torah."
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "לְכָל בְּשָׂרוֹ", שֶׁזֶּה נִקְרָא בָּשָׂר – "רָר בְּשָׂרוֹ" (וַיִּקְרָא טו, ג);
— And this is “to all his flesh,” for this organ is called flesh: “his flesh discharges” (Leviticus 15:3);
וּבִקְדוּשָּׁה – "בְּשַׂר קֹדֶשׁ", וּבַהֵיפֶךְ – "בְּשַׂר חֲמוֹרִים", וְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה "לְכָל בְּשָׂרוֹ מַרְפֵּא".
— which in holiness is "holy flesh," and in corruption "the flesh of donkeys," the Torah serving as medicine for all his flesh.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Vayechi 23:182-26:195: “We have learnt that when God is pleased with a righteous man and the herald makes proclamation concerning him thirty days among the righteous in the Garden of Eden, then all the righteous rejoice and go and crown his place in preparation for his coming to take up his abode among them. But if he is sinful, then the herald proclaims concerning him thirty days in Gehinnom, and all the sinners are sad and exclaim: ‘Woe, that a new punishment is to be executed on so-and-so’, and the demons are ready to meet him. Woe to the wicked and woe to his neighbour!’ Then they all exclaim: ‘Woe to the wicked, it shall be ill with him, for the reward of his hands shall be given to him’ (Is. 3, 11).’ R. Isaac said: ‘The word ra’ (ill) in this passage refers especially to him who wilfully spills his seed, like Er the son of Judah. Such a one is thrust down lower than all the others in that world. All others have a chance to ascend, but not he. Is he even worse, it may be asked, than a murderer? Even so, because a murderer kills another man’s children, but he kills his own, and he spills very much blood. Hence it is written of such a one particularly: ‘And that which he did was evil in the sight of the Lord’ (Gen. 38, 10).’ R. Judah said: ‘Every sin admits of repentance barring this, and every sinner may hope to see the face of the Shekinah barring this one.’ R. Isaac said: ‘Happy are the righteous in this world and in the world to come; of them it is written: ‘And thy people are all righteous, they shall for ever inherit the land (Is. 60, 21).”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Bechukosai 13:1: “The close of the haftarah, ‘Heal me, Hashem, and I shall be healed’: there are sins from which teshuvah is withheld, such as the blemish of the covenant (Zohar I 219b), and we have said that this is because teshuvah, which comes from Binah, does not avail; but Torah, which comes forth from Chochmah (Zohar II 121a), avails even for this. Of this it is said, ‘and healing to all his flesh’: this organ is called flesh, as it says, ‘his flesh runs with his issue’; among Israel it is called holy flesh, and in the opposite, flesh of donkeys. This is in the manner of what they said (Rosh Hashanah 18a): by sacrifice and offering it is not atoned, but it is atoned through Torah. … And this is ‘Heal me, Hashem, and I shall be healed’: ‘heal me’ to repair the past, ‘and I shall be healed’ in the future. For a person’s inclination grows stronger and renews itself every day, and were it not that the Holy One, blessed be He, helps him, he could not withstand it (Sukkah 52a); and once the past is repaired, one merits Hashem’s help for the future: ‘Save me and I shall be saved,’ in the manner of ‘my salvation – on Yom Kippur.’”

h: The Oral Torah Subdues the Inclination

p: וְכֵן עַל הֶעָתִיד לִכְבּוֹשׁ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע וּלְהִתְגַּבֵּר עָלָיו,
— And so too looking to the future, to conquer the yetzer hara and overcome it,
אִיתָא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א, רב עַמּוּד א):
— it is taught (Zohar Part I, 202a):
"דְּהָא לֵית לָךְ מִלָּה לְמִתְבַּר יֵצֶר הָרָע אֶלָּא אוֹרַיְיתָא", וְהַיְינוּ בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם: "יִשְׁתַּדַּל בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא".
— "there is nothing to shatter the evil inclination except Torah," referring to exertion in the Oral Torah.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר: "וּשְׁאַבְתֶּם מַיִם בְּשָׂשׂוֹן" (יְשַׁעְיָה יב, ג) –
— And this is what Scripture continues: "Therefore with joy shall you draw water" (Isaiah 12:3)—
אֵין מַיִם אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה (בָּבָא קַמָּא יז עַמּוּד א),
— water being Torah;
וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הוּא שֶׁנֶּמְשַׁל לְמַיִם,
— and the Oral Torah specifically is compared to water,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (תַּעֲנִית ז עַמּוּד א): שֶׁהֵם כְּמַיִם שֶׁמַּנִּיחִין מָקוֹם גָּבוֹהַּ וְהוֹלְכִים לְמָקוֹם נָמוּךְ.
— in that it leaves high places and flows to the lowest ground (the humble disciple);
וְכֵן נִדְרַשׁ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר "הוֹי כָּל צָמֵא לְכוּ לַמַּיִם" (יְשַׁעְיָה נה, א), וּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "הָתָיוּ מַיִם" – בְּתַלְמִידִים.
— and so "Ho, every one that thirsts, come to the waters" is expounded regarding students gathering to learn.
וְזֶה יִתָּכֵן בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁצָּרִיךְ רַב, וְהֵם מַנִּיחִין מָקוֹם גָּבוֹהַּ וְכוּלֵי;
— And this dynamic applies uniquely to the Oral Torah which requires a master from whom the waters flow downward;
אֲבָל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב – כְּרוּכָה וּמוּנַּחַת בְּקֶרֶן זָוִית, כָּל הָרוֹצֶה לִלְמוֹד יָבֹא וְיִלְמוֹד (קִדּוּשִׁין סו עַמּוּד א).
— whereas the Written Torah lies bound in a corner, open for anyone who wishes to read directly (Kiddushin 66a).

h: The Dew of Torah Revives and Restores

p: וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "מִמַּעַיְנֵי הַיְשׁוּעָה" –
— And this is: "out of the springs of salvation"—
שֶׁהַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה מִטַּלָּא דְּעַתִּיקָא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "תִּזַּל כַּטַּל אִמְרָתִי" (דְּבָרִים לב, ב),
— for the Oral Torah derives from the dew of the Ancient of Days (Talla d'Atika), as it is said: "My speech shall distill as the dew",
וְהֵם חַיֵּי עוֹלָם – טַל שֶׁעָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהַחֲיוֹת בּוֹ מֵתִים,
— which is the dew of resurrection wherewith the Holy One will resurrect the dead,
שֶׁעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (כְּתוּבּוֹת קיא עַמּוּד ב): "כָּל הַמִּשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בְּאוֹר תּוֹרָה – אוֹר תּוֹרָה מְחַיֵּיהוּ",
— concerning which they taught in Ketubot (111b): "Whoever utilizes the light of Torah, the light of Torah revives him",
וּבְתִקּוּנֵי זֹהַר (תִּיקּוּן יט, מא עַמּוּד א) הוּבָא: "טַל תּוֹרָה מְחַיֵּיהוּ",
— and in Tikkunei Zohar (Tikkun 19): "the dew of Torah revives him",
וְהַיְינוּ טַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, טַלָּא דְּעַתִּיקָא.
— which is the dew of the Oral Torah flowing from Atika.
וְזֶהוּ "מִמַּעַיְנֵי הַיְשׁוּעָה" – יְשׁוּעָה עַל הֶעָבָר;
— And this is "from the springs of salvation"—salvation over the past;
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת פט עַמּוּד ב):
— in line with what the Sages stated (Shabbat 89b):
"'אִם יִהְיוּ חֲטָאֵיכֶם כַּשָּׁנִים' (יְשַׁעְיָה א, יח) – כַּשָּׁנִים הַלָּלוּ שֶׁסְּדוּרוֹת וּבָאוֹת מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית",
— "'Though your sins be as scarlet (shanim)'—even if they be like these continuous years (shanim) since the six days of Creation",
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁבְּמַאֲמַר בְּרֵאשִׁית הוּזְכַּר "תֹּהוּ וָבֹהוּ", שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז עַל מַעֲשֵׂיהֶן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (ב, ה);
— meaning that in the account of Genesis "chaos and void" was inscribed, alluding to the deeds of the wicked (Bereishit Rabbah 2:5);
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁכֵּן עָלָה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה "טוֹב מְאֹד",
— so that it arose in the Supernal Thought from the outset in order to culminate in "very good",
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ: "דְּלֵית נְהוֹרָא אֶלָּא הַהוּא דְּנָפֵיק מִגּוֹ חֲשׁוֹכָא, וְלֵית טוֹב וְכוּלֵי",
— in the manner of the Zohar: "there is no light except that which emerges out of darkness, and no good except, etc.",
וּמִזֶּה בָּא הַיְשׁוּעָה עַל הֶעָבָר,
— and from this comes salvation over the past,
שֶׁיּוֹעִיל תְּשׁוּבָה מֵאַהֲבָה שֶׁיִּהְיוּ זְדוֹנוֹת כִּזְכִיּוֹת (יוֹמָא פו עַמּוּד ב),
— wherein repentance out of love transforms willful sins into actual merits (Yoma 86b),
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כַּשֶּׁלֶג יַלְבִּינוּ", וְזֶהוּ "מִמַּעַיְנֵי הַיְשׁוּעָה":
— and concerning this it is promised: "they shall be as white as snow"—which is the wellspring of salvation:

paragraphs.text: Ketubot 111b: “Rabbi Yoḥanan said to Rabbi Elazar: Their master, i.e. God, is not pleased that you say this of ordinary Jews. Rather, that verse is written about one who weakens himself and succumbs to idol worship. Those who commit this great sin do not merit to be resurrected in the future. Rabbi Elazar said to him: I teach it from a different verse, as it is written: ‘For Your dew is as the dew of light, and the earth shall bring to life the shades’ (Isaiah 26:19). Rabbi Elazar explains: Anyone who uses the light of Torah, which is called the dew of light, the light of Torah will revive him; and anyone who does not use the light of Torah, the light of Torah will not revive him.”

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 2:5: “Rabbi Abbahu and Rabbi Chiyya the Great expounded this. Rabbi Abbahu said: From the beginning of creation, the Holy One, blessed be He, foresaw the deeds of the righteous and the deeds of the wicked, as it says, ‘The Lord knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked shall perish.’ ‘The earth was waste and void’ refers to the deeds of the wicked; ‘God said, Let there be light’ refers to the deeds of the righteous. Yet I do not know which He desires—the deeds of these or the deeds of those. Once it says, ‘God saw that the light was good,’ we know that He desires the deeds of the righteous and does not desire the deeds of the wicked.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Shoftim 12:1: “The intent is that the fire came from the first utterance, the utterance ‘In the beginning,’ which corresponds to Keter Elyon: that is, that everything will be repaired, in the manner of what they said (Shabbat 89b), ‘If your sins are like these years (shanim) that are ordered and come from the six days of Creation, they shall be white as snow,’ so that they become like merits. … In the utterance ‘In the beginning’ ‘chaos and void’ is mentioned, which alludes to the deeds of the wicked (Bereishit Rabbah 2), for so was the world created, so that out of everything there should come to be the aspect of ‘very good,’ according to what is said (Zohar II 184a): ‘For there is no light except that which comes forth from within darkness, and no good except that which comes forth from within evil.’ … ‘For He has torn and He will heal us’: healing refers to the past, and it is through Torah, of which it is written ‘and healing to all his flesh,’ and through teshuvah, ‘pour out your heart like water before the face of Hashem.’ ‘He has smitten and He will bind us up’ refers to the future, that it should not be spoiled again.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: Shoftim 12 joins the same sources: the sins “like these years” from Creation, the “chaos and void” of the wicked, the Zohar’s light from within darkness, and “healing to all his flesh.” It applies them to the healing of the past through Torah and teshuvah and the binding up for the future, which matches this os’s salvation over the past and strength for the coming week.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Tetzaveh 10:86: “Besides, the words of the Torah can best sink into the soul there in the desert, for there is no light except that which issues from darkness, for when that ‘other side’ is subdued the Holy One is exalted in glory. In fact, there can be no true worship except it issue forth from darkness, and no true good except it proceed from evil. And when a man enters upon an evil way and then forsakes it the Holy One is exalted in glory. Hence the perfection of all things is attained when good and evil are first of all commingled, and then become all good, for there is no good so perfect as that which issues out of evil. The divine Glory is extolled and extended thereby, and therein lies the essence of perfect worship.”

paragraphs.text: Yoma 86b: “Reish Lakish said: Great is repentance, as the penitent’s intentional sins are counted for him as unwitting transgressions, as it is stated: ‘Return, Israel, to the Lord your God, for you have stumbled in your iniquity’ (Hosea 14:2). The Gemara analyzes this: Doesn’t ‘iniquity’ mean an intentional sin? Yet the prophet calls it stumbling, implying that one who repents is considered as though he only stumbled accidentally in his transgression. The Gemara asks: Is that so? Didn’t Reish Lakish himself say: Great is repentance, as one’s intentional sins are counted for him as merits, as it is stated: ‘And when the wicked turns from his wickedness, and does that which is lawful and right, he shall live thereby’ (Ezekiel 33:19), and all his deeds, even his transgressions, will become praiseworthy? The Gemara reconciles: This is not difficult: Here, when one repents out of love, his sins become like merits; there, when one repents out of fear, his sins are counted as unwitting transgressions.”
